AID427 New Trends in Data Science · Project Phase 1 · Technical report

Pima Diabetes Phase 1Screening for diabetes from routine measurements, with a leakage-free evaluation

Ziad Elsayed FouadID 320230025
Mohamed Adham ElhadidiID 320230001
Mohamed Hussien KamalID 320230008

Faculty of Computer Science and Information Technology, Egypt-Japan University of Science and Technology (E-JUST), Alexandria, Egypt

Logistic regression on four routine measurements (pregnancies, 2-hour glucose, BMI and family-history score) reaches a cross-validated ROC-AUC of 0.846 and a mean 5-fold accuracy of 79.2%. Scored once on 154 held-out patients, it reaches AUC 0.811. At the screening threshold it catches 48 of 54 diabetics.

Summary · the three questions this phase had to answer

Three answers

Q1
No

Did nonlinear reduction improve prediction over all 8 features?

With logistic regression as the reference, the best nonlinear option (Isomap, 4 dimensions) loses 0.014 AUC. UMAP-2 loses 0.068 and LLE-2 loses 0.077. Across all seven classifiers the best nonlinear change ranges from −0.026 to +0.001 AUC, which is inside fold-to-fold noise. The embeddings also show no class separation that the original 8 features lack.

Q2
Yes

Did either metaheuristic reach the exhaustive optimum, and at what cost?

Binary PSO found the exact optimum in 10 of 10 seeds, evaluating about 63 of 255 subsets (25% of exhaustive search) in about 3 seconds per run. The GA found it in 5 of 10 seeds with about 44 subsets, and random search in 4 of 10. With only 8 features, exhaustive search (13.5 s) is cheap enough to be the right tool. The metaheuristics are validated against it.

Q3
LR-4

Which pipeline should be presented?

Logistic regression on the 4 PSO-selected measurements, with the screening threshold. It has the best mean outer-CV AUC under a rule fixed in advance. It is statistically tied with logistic regression on all 8 features while needing half the measurements. Its training and validation AUC match (0.850 vs 0.847), and its threshold never saw the test set.

01 · Rubric: data set description, preprocessing (2 pts)

Data and leakage

The old notebook stacked two files, diabetes.csv and pima_indians_diabetes.csv, into 1,536 rows and de-duplicated them to 1,144. The audit shows both files hold the same 768 patients. The "clean" file had filled every missing value with the median of the patient's own diagnosis class, which writes the answer into the features.

Old pipeline
  • 1,144 rows built from two copies of 768 patients
  • Missing insulin filled with 102.5 if healthy and 169.5 if diabetic
  • For those 374 patients, the filled insulin alone predicts the outcome with AUC 1.000
  • 128 of 229 test rows (55.9%) had their own patient in training
  • Model and the 0.35 threshold chosen from test-set tables
This pipeline
  • 768 raw patients, one row each; MD5 matches OpenML's published checksum
  • Matches an independent UCI mirror row by row
  • Zeros in glucose, blood pressure, skin fold, insulin and BMI become missing values
  • Scaling and KNN imputation (k = 5) fitted inside each training fold
  • Test set locked in a vault object that can be opened only once

The original diabetes.csv was not available. Its construction is shown by rebuilding it and reproducing the old notebook's output exactly: 1,144 rows, and every column count and mean within 5 × 10⁻⁷. A byte-level comparison was not possible.

02 · Rubric: 80/20 split, K-fold cross-validation

Protocol

Every rule below was fixed before any model was scored. The same five outer folds are shared by every comparison, so two pipelines are always judged on the same patients.

1 · selectKeep the requested raw columns
2 · recodeInvalid zeros become missing
3 · scaleStandardScaler, fitted on the training fold
4 · imputeKNN imputation, k = 5
5 · reduce / selectFitted on the training fold; unsupervised reducers never see labels
6 · classifyTuning on inner 5-fold CV only
DecisionRule
Test setStratified 20% (154 patients, 54 positive), random_state=42, opened once at the end
Primary metricMean outer 5-fold ROC-AUC; mean 5-fold accuracy reported beside it
FinalistHighest mean CV AUC; ties within 0.001 go to fewer raw measurements, then the simpler model
Screening thresholdHighest threshold with out-of-fold recall ≥ 0.85 on the development set
ParsimonyA feature must earn ≥ 0.002 AUC: forward/backward tolerance, MI-k rule, metaheuristic penalty

Without the leaked insulin values and the duplicated patients, the ranking reverses: tree ensembles memorise the training folds and gain nothing on validation. Nested tuning (inner 5-fold grid search with preprocessing inside) narrows their gaps. Tuned gradient boosting scores 0.834 AUC with a gap of 0.088, but none beats logistic regression.

04 · Rubric: linear reduction (1 pt), non-linear reduction (6 pts), visualization

Dimensionality reduction

Linear. PCA puts 32.2% of variance in PC1 and 19.7% in PC2, and needs 5 components for 80%. Truncated SVD gives the same ratios because the data is already centred by standardisation. Binary LDA has one axis, weighted mainly on glucose (0.91), BMI (0.49) and pregnancies (0.28).

Custom SNE, verified. The from-scratch SNE is symmetric SNE: joint P, joint Gaussian Q, gradient 4Σ(p − q)(yᵢ − yⱼ). Its perplexities hit the target exactly, the gradient matches finite differences (relative error 2 × 10⁻¹⁰), and KL falls from 2.86 to 1.33.

05 · Rubric: visualization before and after clustering

Clustering without labels

K-means was fitted without the outcome; silhouette picked k = 2 (0.21, weak structure). The clusters separate an older, heavier, higher-glucose profile (median age 41, glucose 137, BMI 34.6) from a younger, leaner one (age 25, glucose 105, BMI 30.0). Checked against the diagnosis only afterwards, the first cluster is 58% diabetic and the second 16%. Agreement is still weak (ARI 0.19, NMI 0.15): 118 non-diabetics sit in the "high-risk" cluster. The clusters are risk profiles, not the diagnosis.

06 · Rubric: filter (1 pt), wrapper (2 pts), embedded (2 pts)

Feature selection rules

MethodFamilyRule that produces the subsetChosen on the 614 dev patients
Mutual informationFilterRank by MI; smallest top-k within 0.002 of the best inner-CV AUCall 8 (k = 8)
Forward SFSWrapperAdd features while the gain is ≥ 0.002Pregnancies, Glucose, BMI, DPF
Backward SFSWrapperRemove features while the loss is ≤ 0.002Pregnancies, Glucose, BMI, DPF
RFECVWrapperSize with the best inner-CV AUC6: drops skin fold and insulin
L1 (lasso)EmbeddedC by inner CV (1.0); keep non-zero weights6: drops skin fold and insulin
L2 (ridge)EmbeddedC by inner CV (0.1); keep |coef| ≥ mean |coef|, since L2 never zeroes a weightPregnancies, Glucose, BMI
Elastic Net (l1 ratio 0.5)EmbeddedC by inner CV (0.46); keep non-zero weights6: drops skin fold and insulin

These seven methods select after imputation, so a dropped column still feeds the imputer. They shrink the model's inputs but not the measurements a clinic must take. Only the raw-column searches in the next section drop measurements before imputation.

07 · Rubric: GA and other metaheuristics (2 pts)

GA vs binary PSO, against the exact optimum

All 255 non-empty subsets of the 8 raw columns are scored by one objective: mean 5-fold CV AUC of the full pipeline, minus 0.002 per feature. Exhaustive search gives the exact optimum. GA (tournament selection, single-point crossover, bit-flip mutation, elitism), binary PSO (sigmoid transfer, constriction coefficients) and random search each get the same folds and the same budget of 80 objective calls. Each runs with ten fixed seeds.

Logistic-regression objective · each dot is one seed · filled = reached the exact optimum {Pregnancies, Glucose, BMI, DPF}

The top of the landscape is flat: ten subsets lie within 0.004 of each other. Glucose, BMI and pregnancies appear in every good subset, and the logistic-regression objective never needs insulin or skin fold. That reverses the old finding that insulin was "selected by every method", which came from the leaked insulin values. Inside the nested folds (one seed each), the GA hit the inner optimum in 3 of 5 folds and PSO in 2 of 5; every miss was within 0.003 and left outer AUC unchanged.

08 · Comparison: all 8 vs linear vs nonlinear vs selected features

Prediction on identical folds

Every representation is fitted inside each outer training fold and applied to the untouched validation fold. Only reducers that can map new patients are scored: PCA, SVD, LDA, Kernel PCA, Isomap, LLE and UMAP. SNE, t-SNE and MDS cannot map new patients, so they stay in the embedding comparison. The reference classifier is logistic regression.

Raw-column search (fewer measurements) Filter / wrapper / embedded Linear reduction Nonlinear reduction

Change in mean outer 5-fold ROC-AUC relative to all 8 features (0.844). The fold-to-fold SD of the differences is 0.002–0.11, so anything inside ±0.005 is a tie.

False negatives · the costly error

At 0.5 the model misses 27 of 54 diabetics. Their profile looks healthy: median glucose 123 mg/dL versus 164 for the diabetics it catches, BMI 32.0 versus 36.6, age 32 versus 38. The screening threshold catches 21 of the 27 for 17 extra false alarms. The 6 still missed have glucose of 78–129, and 4 of them lack insulin or skin-fold values.

False positives · the cheaper error

The 20 false alarms at 0.5 look diabetic: median glucose 153.5 mg/dL and BMI 37.5. In screening, each one costs a confirmatory glucose test. Some may be early or undiagnosed cases, but the data cannot show that.

Why test is lower than CV

After the finalist was locked, four other pipelines were refitted and scored on the same 154 patients. This could not change the choice.

The corrected 79% cross-validated accuracy falls in the 77–80% range of the verified single-classifier studies. The old 87.8% sat 8–10 points above that range, which is consistent with the leakage found in section 01.

11 · Reconciliation with the 2026-11-21 notebook

What changed

Historical claimNow
Gradient boosting on 5 tree-GA features: accuracy 0.878, AUC 0.942Withdrawn. Re-estimated with nested CV, that pipeline scores accuracy 0.759, AUC 0.829
Screening threshold 0.35 with recall 0.938Replaced. It was read off the test set; 0.235 is chosen out-of-fold, giving test recall 0.889
Two public versions merged into 1,144 reliable rowsWithdrawn. They are the same 768 patients, and one version leaks the label
Tree ensembles lead every rankingReversed. Logistic regression leads; tree ensembles overfit
Insulin selected by every methodReversed. No logistic-regression-based selector needs insulin
No quantitative embedding comparisonAdded: trustworthiness at three neighbourhood sizes, label agreement and runtime
